pr_title: ES|QL: better management of exact subfields for TEXT fields
pr_body:
Fixes https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/99899

For a mapping like:
```
"field": {
    "type": "text",
    "fields": {
        "raw":{
            "type":"keyword",
        }
    }
},
```

and a query like

```
FROM idx | sort text | where text == "foo" | keep text
```

ESQL optimizer can decide to use the subfield `text.raw` rather than the original `text` field, for performance reasons that include:
- fetch performance 
- ability to push sort and filter operations down to Lucene

There are cases though when the subfield value is not exactly the same as the original one (eg. because of `ignore_above` or `normalizer).
This PR improves the detection of these cases, so that the subfield is used only when it's really accurate.

issue_context.title: ESQL: better management of exact subfields
issue_context.body:
ESQL uses exact [subfields](https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/current/multi-fields.html) in a few different situations:
- for optimization, eg. a `KEYWORD` subfield can be used to avoid extracting `TEXT` from source, 
- when the original value is not available, eg. with synthetic source

Current API, ie. `EsField.getExactField/Info()` and `FieldAttribute.exactAttribute()/getExactInfo()`, does not take into consideration a few important factors:
- in case of multiple exact subfields, it just returns none
- it ignores the fact that the subfield value could be different from the original one, eg. because of specific mapping options like `ignore_above` or `normalizer`

Moreover, the substitution of TEXT fields with their subfields is not performed in all cases, so the planning needs a second  check to make it more consistent.

In some situations it can lead to incorrect results and to sub-optimal performance. 
Some ESQL warnings could also be misleading, eg. in case of synthetic source and  multiple subfields, the warning will still be `Field [fieldname] cannot be retrieved, it is unsupported or not indexed; returning null` that is not completely accurate, since the field value could actually be available in one of the subfields.

This method should probably have a name like `canUseSyntheticSourceDelegateForQuerying`.

Oh! There's no use in using the delegate for querying if the field isn't indexed. maybe check that?

And! I'm not 100% sure block loading works for synthetic source keyword fields with doc values disabled. We *should* fall to the `originalName()` stored field. If we don't that's a bug.
